decisions.reason: After several years the polymer-concrete drain housing is likely embedded in the firm's drainage families, and management can justify continued support through its strong portfolio fit while attributing any weaker uptake to temporary construction-market disruptions.
As the publicly emphasized designer shower drainage flagship aligned with the firm's stated future direction, it carries the strongest visible commitment and is very unlikely to be withdrawn.

Although less prominently presented than some other launches, the shower element with integrated slope directly supports the firm's low-profile, renovation-friendly installation strategy, so management would more likely persist than reverse course.

The backflow-protected basement floor drain reflects the firm's engineering-led problem solving and received a dedicated launch push, making withdrawal possible but still unlikely without unmistakably persistent underperformance.
